public_rationale: The quotation expressly mentions six years, ending December 8, 2031. No early event meeting the investment-recovery rule was established. [Oracle reported 32% AI-capacity gross margin](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/orcl/transcripts/529436-q3-2026/), which is material counterevidence to a gross-margin reading. It does not establish cumulative recovery of the capital expenditure discussed in context. The choice of profit measure matters and must remain visible to reviewers.
limitations: A gross-margin interpretation could produce a different assessment.
The evidence is management's disclosure reproduced by a transcript provider, not audited deployment accounts.
The scope of the relevant GPU investments is unspecified.

our_interpretation: In the surrounding discussion of recovering capital expenditure, the ordinary reading concerns whether AI GPU deployments can earn back their attributable capital and operating costs.
The exact quotation supplies a six-year testing window despite the supplied normalized horizon being null. Three years is the shorter comparison.
The present-tense profitability assertion is a premise within the broader forecast; it is not separately resolved here.
The cited Oracle example uses gross margin, which is a plausible alternative reading of profit. A positive quarterly gross margin does not by itself establish cumulative recovery of deployment costs.
The estimate accounting basis follows the press-report example. No GAAP, IFRS or company-reported basis is specified for the broader forecast.
criteria.support_condition: By December 8, 2031, sufficiently comprehensive deployment-level accounts show that the relevant AI GPU investments failed to recover their attributable capital and operating costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible accounts establish that a relevant big-tech AI GPU deployment recovered its attributable capital and operating costs and earned a positive cumulative surplus within the six-year window.
